snippets.snippet_text: "In 2019, when Diego was responding to students, he earned $8-$10 for every course enrollment. He stopped 3-4 years later, when he was getting 5-50 cents for most students. By June 2025, his monthly payouts weren't much, but he still got something out of his course before the payment halt."

"For the last two or three years, my course, which took months to develop, has been sold for less than a euro (0.99€), and people get the course without really knowing clearly that they pay a yearly subscription. Domestika is winning two times because they're charging users a high subscription fee (say 200€) after paying 0.99€, and we receive 25% of 0.99€. So that's a really nasty move. Now, they're not even paying my royalties since the last five months."

"Over the years, she'd stayed silent about her lack of rights over her course. Plus, her affiliate link that gave her 75% commission as opposed to the 25% (if they signed up through Domestika) kept changing or breaking (which she believed was intentional). These student discounts barely earned her $10-$15 every month. She felt helpless because her primary contact had stopped responding to her emails."

"(Earlier) The team was great, and my first two courses didn't even have a contract. They did all the production, helped me set up my first course, and it even became a best-seller. Then they started to downgrade these royalties. Their last proposal was 5% (royalties) for a new course, which I refused."

"At first, some of the people were asking for the payment, and I thought there must be a delay, but then we got an email from CGMA saying that, for legal reasons, Domestika had forced them to seize all communications with CGMA instructors. I thought, 'Okay, this is bad.'"

"Domestika hasn't stopped paying every inactive instructor. Liam Filler*, a Florida-based instructor, has been getting paid until now, despite not replying to students for a year and a half. He, too, like Diego, launched his course around 2019. The reason why Domestika has targeted some while paying others is unknown. The only difference I spotted is that Liam lives in the U.S. (where Domestika's office is), while the others are based outside."

"In August 2025, when Diego Gomez*, a Madrid-based Domestika instructor, checked his instructor dashboard, he found that the billion-dollar company had stopped paying him since July. The reason was his inactivity in the forum. He didn't understand why the online creative learning platform had halted his payments now. He had stopped replying to comments four years ago (his contract never stated it as a payment condition), and he was still getting paid until June 2025."
"They answered that we can have a video call, I said no as I just wanted a written answer saying if they are going to pay or not. Since then, no more replies."
"After the acquisition, Brienne Gil*, a CGMA instructor, mentioned that Domestika asked the instructors to market their own courses, which led to a drop in enrollments."

"Your students are waiting for you! We have temporarily paused your commission due to a period of inactivity in the forum and course comments. But don't worry: your classroom is still open and your students are hoping to hear from you. As soon as we see that you're available for your students and participating regularly in your course community during the next 90 days, your commissions will automatically reactivate. Come back and reconnect: your guidance makes all the difference! Go to your Community →"

"Denzel Alvares* has two courses on the platform. One was shot in 2016 (without a contract), in his own apartment. The other one, in 2020, was shot in a 'state-of-the-art' studio in a 'fantastic' three-story building in Madrid. He remembered the organized chaos of the space; the team was shooting for multiple courses simultaneously. They were launching more and launching fast."

Class Central investigative report (November 4, 2025) on Domestika unpaid instructors. 11 snippets from multiple pseudonymous instructors (Diego Gomez/Madrid, Denzel Alvares, Brienne Gil/CGMA, Liam Filler/Florida). Richest source in this shard.

Key data points: Diego earned $8-10/enrollment in 2019 → 5-50 cents later → payment halted July 2025. Course priced 0.99€ with 25% royalty to instructor. Affiliate link offers 75% vs 25% direct. New forum activity clause: 90-day window to reactivate commissions.
net_vs_gross_ambiguity: royalty percentages (25% standard, 75% affiliate, 5% new proposal) do not specify net or gross revenue basis.
checkout_vs_payout_ambiguity: 0.99€ is the checkout price; instructor payout is 25% of that. SNP-002 mixes checkout and payout figures.
current_vs_historical_ambiguity: spans 2016 through November 2025; historical earnings and current payment halt both appear across snippets.
Geographic observation in SNP-006: Florida-based instructor continued receiving payments while European-based instructors did not; possible jurisdictional dimension.
